purpose: Gauge-first research decisions for the initial West Virginia route cohort. This is a research artifact, not live route data.

gaugeDecisions.reason: Fresh discharge and stage are available. American Whitewater ties the gauge directly to its Bluestone-Dam-to-Sandstone reach with a 1.35-5.0 foot runnable range, and NPS confirms multiple public access points within that reach. The selected candidate stops at Hellems Beach and therefore does not cross the mandatory Sandstone Falls portage.

Fresh discharge and stage are available. American Whitewater publishes gauge-specific numeric ranges for the Sandstone-McCreery, McCreery-Thurmond, Thurmond-Cunard, and Cunard-Fayette Station reaches. NPS independently confirms the named public access chain and distinguishes the intermediate upper river from the advanced/expert river below Thurmond.

Fresh discharge and stage are available. NPS publishes an exact 4-7 foot safe navigation range on the Pipestem gauge and recognizes the Pipestem-to-Bluestone-State-Park paddling corridor. The current candidate remains operationally blocked until the new tram's private-boat carriage policy is explicit.

Fresh discharge and stage are available, but no selected reach has a route-specific numeric relationship to the Durbin station. American Whitewater uses the downstream Buckeye gauge for the Durbin-to-Hosterman reach, so Durbin may corroborate local conditions but must not drive scoring without calibration.

Fresh discharge and stage are available. American Whitewater publishes Buckeye-stage ranges for multiple upper Greenbrier reaches, including Spring Creek to Anthony, whose endpoints WVDNR independently lists as boat-access sites.

Fresh discharge and stage are available. American Whitewater publishes a 2.85-10 foot range for the Ronceverte-to-Fort-Spring and Fort-Spring-to-Alderson reaches, and WVDNR lists each selected endpoint as boat access.

Fresh discharge and stage are available. American Whitewater publishes Hilldale-stage ranges for Talcott to Willowwood and the adjacent lower reach; WVDNR confirms the selected access chain. The lower Willowwood/Bellepoint candidate remains blocked by conflicting endpoint names and coordinates.

Fresh discharge and stage are available. American Whitewater directly associates the gauge with the Class I-II Seven Islands reach and publishes a 500-8,000 cfs range. WVDNR and the Upper Cheat River Water Trail independently confirm the public access chain.

gaugeDecisions.stationName: Elk River below Webster Springs, WV
gaugeDecisions.reason: Fresh discharge and stage are available. American Whitewater ties the station directly to the 17.5-mile Webster Springs downriver reach and publishes a 4.5-8.0 foot runnable range. This is the strongest threshold-ready Elk backbone station.
potentialRoutes: Sandy Beach to the CR 7/Clifton Ford bridge

gaugeDecisions.reason: Fresh discharge and stage are available on the approved Elk River Water Trail. Frametown is an identified river/trail access, so the station can directly support adjacent access-pair research; a route-specific numeric range remains the next threshold gate.
potentialRoutes: Frametown Bridge access pairs on the Elk River Water Trail

gaugeDecisions.stationName: Elk River at Queen Shoals, WV
gaugeDecisions.reason: Fresh discharge and stage are available at a WV State Parks/WVDNR public launch. The station can directly support King Shoals, Queen Shoals, and Clendenin access-pair research; numeric route thresholds remain unqualified.

Fresh discharge and stage are available at the downstream end of the approved Elk River Water Trail. State and trail sources identify lower-river launches through Blue Creek and Charleston, making the station direct for urban access-pair research; Mink Shoals is currently marked closed and must not be used.
potentialRoutes: Blue Creek to Charleston access pairs, excluding closed Mink Shoals

gaugeDecisions.stationName: Cacapon River near Great Cacapon, WV
gaugeDecisions.reason: Fresh discharge and stage are available. American Whitewater publishes the station as an explicit secondary correlation for the Capon Bridge-to-WV 127 reach at 550-7,000 cfs, while WVDNR and water-trail sources document public access along the river.

gaugeDecisions.stationName: Big Coal River at Ashford, WV
gaugeDecisions.reason: Fresh discharge and stage are available. The 2026 Coal River Water Trail brochure publishes a multi-access Big Coal route chain, and American Whitewater links the station to both the Whitesville mainstem reach and upstream Marsh Fork whitewater. Direct mainstem cards should be researched separately from upstream proxy uses.

gaugeDecisions.stationName: Little Coal River at Danville, WV
gaugeDecisions.reason: Fresh discharge and stage are available within the branch-specific route chain published in the 2026 Coal River Water Trail brochure. Madison, Danville, and downstream public launches make the station direct for bounded Little Coal candidates; numeric thresholds still need qualification.
potentialRoutes: Danville to Donald R. Kuhn access

gaugeDecisions.reason: Fresh discharge and stage are available on the combined Coal River. The 2026 trail brochure publishes public segments through Meadowood Park, Lower Falls, and St. Albans, with an explicit dam/portage warning that must be treated as a hard route boundary.

gaugeDecisions.stationName: West Fork River below Stonewall Jackson Dam near Weston, WV
gaugeDecisions.reason: Fresh discharge and stage are available immediately below a WVDNR-listed public tailwater access on the approved West Fork River Water Trail. The station is direct, but any scored route must model regulation and release changes rather than assume natural-flow behavior.
potentialRoutes: Stonewall tailwater to the next verified West Fork public access

gaugeDecisions.stationName: West Fork River at Butcherville, WV
gaugeDecisions.reason: Fresh discharge and stage are available on the approved West Fork River Water Trail. The gauge is direct for nearby access-pair research, but public endpoint coordinates and numeric thresholds remain to be joined.
potentialRoutes: Butcherville-area West Fork public access pairs

gaugeDecisions.stationName: West Fork River near Mount Clare, WV
gaugeDecisions.reason: Fresh discharge and stage are available on the approved water trail. Current watershed work documents water-trail signage and obstruction checks near Mount Clare, supporting direct local route research; official endpoints and thresholds remain to be joined.

gaugeDecisions.stationName: West Fork River at Enterprise, WV
gaugeDecisions.reason: Fresh discharge and stage are available. WVDNR publishes a five-mile Worthington-to-Monongah public float and AW maintains that Class I-II reach; the downstream Enterprise station is a same-river proxy that AW uses for the route and therefore has candidate value, subject to threshold qualification.

Fresh discharge and stage are available upstream of Summersville Lake. American Whitewater ties the station directly to Camden-on-Gauley-to-Curtin Bridge and publishes route guidance beginning around 11 feet. This gauge supports natural-flow upper Gauley research only; it must not be used for Gauley Season below the dam.

Fresh discharge and stage are available far downstream in the Gauley system. The station can corroborate broad lower-river conditions, but it cannot replace the discontinued below-Summersville-Dam USGS station or model the timing and magnitude of scheduled releases through the Upper and Lower Gauley reaches.

gauleyLiveProviderDecision.repositoryConstraint: The application GaugeProvider union and fetch dispatcher currently support only USGS and Minnesota DNR; they do not support USACE CWMS.
gauleyLiveProviderDecision.releaseModel: A scheduled release is a time-bounded operating plan, not an ordinary observed-gauge threshold. A future Gauley implementation must combine current USACE outflow, a current-year primary USACE schedule, delay/travel-time rules for lower reaches, cancellation/change handling, and advanced/expert safety gating.
gauleyLiveProviderDecision.routeDecision: Do not include Summersville-Dam-to-Woods-Ferry or the Lower Gauley in the initial scored cohort. The NPS page available during this review still displays the 2025 schedule, so it is not valid as the 2026 schedule source. Permit planning-only release content only when it is visibly dated and linked to the current primary USACE schedule.
gauleyLiveProviderDecision.upstreamException: USGS 03189100 remains route-capable for natural-flow Gauley reaches upstream of Summersville Lake; it is not a release proxy.

initialCohort.selectionRule: Only candidates marked advance, with two official or officially listed endpoints, a numeric gauge decision, explicit safety notes, and a camping classification are included.
implementationGuardrails: All 12 remain routeType whitewater under repository rules because they are Class II-or-higher and/or use American Whitewater as the primary threshold source.
Do not convert the broad AW runnable maxima directly into Paddle Today safe maxima without the conservative calibration noted in each dossier.
Re-run current closures, access status, and gauge freshness during the implementation batch; current observations are intentionally not frozen into route data.
